name: Paul, at the end of his course
charge: I have fought a good fight, I have finished my course, I have kept the faith
summary: Paul wrote his last letter knowing he was ready to be offered and that the time of his departure was at hand (2 Timothy 4:6). He said he had fought a good fight, finished his course, and kept the faith, and that a crown of righteousness was laid up for him, which the Lord the righteous judge would give him at that day, and not to him only but to all them also that love his appearing (2 Timothy 4:7-8). At his first answer no man stood with him, yet the Lord stood with him and strengthened him (2 Timothy 4:16-17).
offenseFull: Paul was not guessing about the ending. Christ had said of him at the very beginning that he was a chosen vessel to bear his name before the Gentiles and kings and the children of Israel, and that he would be shown how great things he must suffer for that name (Acts 9:15-16), and Peter likewise knew he must shortly put off his tabernacle because Christ had showed him (2 Peter 1:14). So when Paul told the elders at Miletus that bonds and afflictions awaited him in every city, he could add that none of these things moved him, neither counted he his life dear to himself, so that he might finish his course with joy and the ministry he had received (Acts 20:22-24). He was not out to preserve his life; he was out to finish the work, because the man who saves his life loses it.

The course is itemised: stripes above measure, prisons more frequent, deaths often, five times forty stripes save one, three times beaten with rods, once stoned, three shipwrecks, a night and a day in the deep, perils of waters, of robbers, of his own countrymen, of the heathen, in the city, in the wilderness, in the sea, among false brethren, and on top of all of it the care of all the churches daily (2 Corinthians 11:23-28). The stoning at Lystra was the worst of it: they drew him out of the city supposing he was dead, and he rose up and went back in (Acts 14:19-20). The teaching sets that hour beside the man caught up to the third heaven, into paradise, who heard unspeakable words not lawful for a man to utter (2 Corinthians 12:2-4). Paul counted himself the least of the apostles, not fit to be called one because he persecuted the congregation of God, and said he laboured more abundantly than they all, yet not he but the grace of God with him (1 Corinthians 15:9-10): he did more work because he had done more damage. He forgot the things behind and reached toward the mark for the prize of the high calling (Philippians 3:13-14), and kept his own body under, lest after preaching to others he himself should be a castaway (1 Corinthians 9:24-27).
judgmentFull: He had fought a good fight, finished his course, and kept the faith, and there was laid up for him a crown of righteousness which the Lord the righteous judge would give him at that day (2 Timothy 4:7-8). The crown is not his alone. It is promised to all them also that love his appearing, which puts it in front of everybody who actually wants that day to come.

The ending itself was lonely. At his first answer no man stood with him and all men forsook him, and he prayed that it would not be laid to their charge (2 Timothy 4:16). Demas had gone, Crescens was in Galatia, Titus in Dalmatia, and only Luke was with him (2 Timothy 4:10-11). Notwithstanding, the Lord stood with him and strengthened him, so that by him the preaching might be fully known and all the Gentiles hear, and he was delivered out of the mouth of the lion (2 Timothy 4:17). He said the Lord would deliver him from every evil work and preserve him to his heavenly kingdom (2 Timothy 4:18). He had also left the elders at Ephesus a clean account of how he had lived among them: he coveted no man’s silver, gold, or apparel, his own hands ministered to his necessities and to them that were with him, and he taught them that it is more blessed to give than to receive (Acts 20:33-35). He was beheaded at Rome under Nero soon after the letter was sent.

text.text: For I am now ready to be offered, and the time of my departure is at hand.
But the Lord said unto him, Go thy way: for he is a chosen vessel unto me, to bear my name before the Gentiles, and kings, and the children of Israel:
For I will shew him how great things he must suffer for my name’s sake.
Knowing that shortly I must put off this my tabernacle, even as our Lord Jesus Christ hath shewed me.
And now, behold, I go bound in the spirit unto Jerusalem, not knowing the things that shall befall me there:
Save that the Holy Ghost witnesseth in every city, saying that bonds and afflictions abide me.

But none of these things move me, neither count I my life dear unto myself, so that I might finish my course with joy, and the ministry, which I have received of the Lord Jesus, to testify the gospel of the grace of God.
Are they ministers of Christ? (I speak as a fool) I am more; in labours more abundant, in stripes above measure, in prisons more frequent, in deaths oft.
Of the Jews five times received I forty stripes save one.
Thrice was I beaten with rods, once was I stoned, thrice I suffered shipwreck, a night and a day I have been in the deep;

In journeyings often, in perils of waters, in perils of robbers, in perils by mine own countrymen, in perils by the heathen, in perils in the city, in perils in the wilderness, in perils in the sea, in perils among false brethren;
In weariness and painfulness, in watchings often, in hunger and thirst, in fastings often, in cold and nakedness.
Beside those things that are without, that which cometh upon me daily, the care of all the churches.
And there came thither certain Jews from Antioch and Iconium, who persuaded the people, and, having stoned Paul, drew him out of the city, supposing he had been dead.
Howbeit, as the disciples stood round about him, he rose up, and came into the city: and the next day he departed with Barnabas to Derbe.
I knew a man in Christ above fourteen years ago, (whether in the body, I cannot tell; or whether out of the body, I cannot tell: God knoweth;) such an one caught up to the third heaven.
And I knew such a man, (whether in the body, or out of the body, I cannot tell: God knoweth;)
How that he was caught up into paradise, and heard unspeakable words, which it is not lawful for a man to utter.
For I am the least of the apostles, that am not meet to be called an apostle, because I persecuted the church of God.
But by the grace of God I am what I am: and his grace which was bestowed upon me was not in vain; but I laboured more abundantly than they all: yet not I, but the grace of God which was with me.
Brethren, I count not myself to have apprehended: but this one thing I do, forgetting those things which are behind, and reaching forth unto those things which are before,
I press toward the mark for the prize of the high calling of God in Christ Jesus.
Know ye not that they which run in a race run all, but one receiveth the prize? So run, that ye may obtain.
And every man that striveth for the mastery is temperate in all things. Now they do it to obtain a corruptible crown; but we an incorruptible.
I therefore so run, not as uncertainly; so fight I, not as one that beateth the air:
But I keep under my body, and bring it into subjection: lest that by any means, when I have preached to others, I myself should be a castaway.
I have fought a good fight, I have finished my course, I have kept the faith:
Henceforth there is laid up for me a crown of righteousness, which the Lord, the righteous judge, shall give me at that day: and not to me only, but unto all them also that love his appearing.
At my first answer no man stood with me, but all men forsook me: I pray God that it may not be laid to their charge.
For Demas hath forsaken me, having loved this present world, and is departed unto Thessalonica; Crescens to Galatia, Titus unto Dalmatia.
Only Luke is with me. Take Mark, and bring him with thee: for he is profitable to me for the ministry.
Notwithstanding the Lord stood with me, and strengthened me; that by me the preaching might be fully known, and that all the Gentiles might hear: and I was delivered out of the mouth of the lion.
And the Lord shall deliver me from every evil work, and will preserve me unto his heavenly kingdom: to whom be glory for ever and ever. Amen.
I have coveted no man’s silver, or gold, or apparel.
Yea, ye yourselves know, that these hands have ministered unto my necessities, and to them that were with me.
I have shewed you all things, how that so labouring ye ought to support the weak, and to remember the words of the Lord Jesus, how he said, It is more blessed to give than to receive.
